## Category: Hardware / Diagnostics

### Battery Discharge & Drain Curve Monitor
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/battery_discharge_monitor
- Summary: Track real-time battery percentage discharge rates, discharge duration estimates, and charging status using the Battery Status API in Chromium on Windows and Android.
- Overview: Record battery discharge curves and calculate runtime projections via the Battery Status API. Supported in Chrome and Edge on Windows, Linux, Android, and ChromeOS to audit background battery drain without installing native utilities.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Unplug Power Adapter: Disconnect your laptop, tablet, or smartphone from AC power to initiate active battery discharge monitoring.
  * Initialize Monitoring Session: Launch the monitor in a supported Chromium browser. The tool reads initial battery level and discharge status.
  * Run Target Workload: Perform your typical tasks (web browsing, coding, video playback, gaming) while the tool logs percentage drop over time.
  * Inspect Discharge Curve: Analyze the computed discharge velocity (% drain per hour) and estimated remaining operating runtime.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is the Battery Status API blocked in Firefox and Safari?
    A: Mozilla and Apple removed navigator.getBattery() in 2016-2017 because researchers demonstrated that high-resolution battery level readings combined with discharge duration could be used to fingerprint users across private browsing sessions.
  * Q: How does this tool calculate battery discharge rate?
    A: The tool samples `battery.level` changes and timestamps at periodic intervals, calculating the rate of change ($Delta Level / Delta Time$) to project battery drain rate (%/hr) and estimated time to depletion.
  * Q: Can web browsers detect battery cycle count or battery health?
    A: No. The W3C Battery Status API intentionally only exposes level (0.0 to 1.0), charging status (boolean), chargingTime (seconds), and dischargingTime (seconds). Hardware cycle count and design capacity (mAh) are protected OS metrics.

### Bluetooth LE Device Scanner & GATT Explorer
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/web_bluetooth_scan
- Summary: Discover nearby Bluetooth Low Energy peripherals and explore available GATT services and characteristics using Web Bluetooth in supported Chromium browsers.
- Overview: Scan for nearby Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) peripherals and inspect GATT services and characteristics in real time. Runs via the Web Bluetooth API in Chrome and Edge on desktop and Android with user-granted Bluetooth permissions.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Verify Browser Support: Open this tool in Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Opera on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, or Android.
  * Request Bluetooth Device: Click 'Scan for BLE Devices' to prompt the browser security dialog. Select the peripheral you wish to pair with.
  * Connect to GATT Server: Establish an authenticated GATT connection to inspect generic access, battery service, device information, and custom UUIDs.
  * Read and Subscribe Characteristics: Read readable characteristic values or subscribe to notifications to observe live incoming telemetry data.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Which web browsers support the Web Bluetooth API?
    A: The Web Bluetooth API is supported in Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Chromium-based browsers on macOS, Windows 10/11, Linux, ChromeOS, and Android. It is not supported in Mozilla Firefox, Apple Safari on iOS or macOS, or Chromium iOS.
  * Q: Can a website scan for Bluetooth devices silently in the background?
    A: No. The W3C Web Bluetooth specification strictly mandates user-initiated interaction. A browser permission picker always appears, requiring the user to explicitly select and authorize the specific device before any communication can occur.
  * Q: What are GATT services and characteristics?
    A: GATT (Generic Attribute Profile) organizes Bluetooth LE data into Services (logical groupings identified by 16-bit or 128-bit UUIDs, e.g. Battery Service 0x180F) and Characteristics (specific data points with read, write, or notify permissions).

### Bluetooth RSSI Signal Strength & Beacon Tracker
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/ble_rssi_meter
- Summary: Track relative signal strength (RSSI) from advertising Bluetooth LE beacons in supported Chromium browsers to estimate proximity and locate nearby devices.
- Overview: Monitor live Bluetooth Low Energy advertisement RSSI values to approximate physical beacon distance and locate nearby hardware. Runs in Chrome on Android and macOS with Bluetooth permissions enabled.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Enable Bluetooth Advertising: Ensure your lost Bluetooth device or beacon is powered on and within broadcast range (typically up to 30 feet / 10 meters).
  * Pair Beacon in Browser: Click 'Track Bluetooth Device' in Google Chrome to authorize connection to the target device's advertisement feed.
  * Monitor Signal Strength Needle: Watch the RSSI decibel-milliwatts (dBm) gauge. Values closer to 0 (e.g. -45 dBm) indicate close proximity; values near -90 dBm indicate weak range.
  * Walk Toward Stronger Signal: Move slowly through rooms. When the RSSI increases and audio beeps accelerate, you are closing in on the physical device location.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can Bluetooth RSSI accurately measure exact distance in meters?
    A: No. Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) is inherently noisy and fluctuates due to radio multi-path fading, physical obstructions (walls, bodies, furniture), and antenna polarization. RSSI indicates proximity trends (getting closer vs further) rather than precise metric distances.
  * Q: What RSSI dBm values correspond to proximity ranges?
    A: Typically, -30 to -50 dBm indicates immediate proximity (within 1 to 2 feet); -50 to -70 dBm indicates medium proximity (same room, 3 to 10 feet); and -75 to -95 dBm indicates distant proximity or signal blockage through walls.
  * Q: Why does Bluetooth signal fluctuate even when neither device moves?
    A: Radio frequency signals in the 2.4GHz ISM band suffer from constructive and destructive interference caused by human movement, domestic Wi-Fi routers, microwave ovens, and physical reflections off metal and mirrors.

### Browser-Based GPU Stress & Thermal Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/gpu_thermal_throttling_test
- Summary: Down It is a common scenario for gamers and creative professionals: you launch a demanding application, and for the first 15 minutes, performance is flawless.
- Overview: Browser-Based GPU Stress & Thermal Test is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Browser-Based GPU Stress & Thermal Test directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can this stress test permanently damage my laptop?
    A: No. Modern processors (manufactured after roughly 2008) have embedded hardware-level thermal trip points (like PROCHOT on Intel/Nvidia chips). If the cooling system completely fails, the hardware will cut its own power and force a system shutdown before physical silicon melting occurs. The worst this tool will do is drain your battery rapidly and spin your fans at maximum volume.
  * Q: Why is my FPS stuck at 60 or 144?
    A: This is V-Sync (Vertical Synchronization). Browsers are typically hard-coded to limit WebGL rendering to your monitor's refresh rate to save power. If you have a 60Hz screen, the test cannot exceed 60 FPS. To test for throttling, increase the "Shader Complexity" slider until your FPS drops below your maximum refresh rate, then monitor it for further drops.
  * Q: Does this work on mobile phones?
    A: Yes. This test uses standard WebGL 1.0/2.0 which is supported by iOS (iPhone) and Android. In fact, mobile phones throttle much faster than PCs because they rely on passive cooling (transferring heat to the glass/metal body) rather than fans. You will often see significant performance drops on phones within 60 seconds of running this test at high intensity.

### Compute Pressure CPU Monitor
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/compute_pressure_monitor
- Summary: Monitor real-time CPU compute pressure states (nominal, fair, serious, critical) via the W3C Compute Pressure API. Audit thermal throttling risk in browser memory.
- Overview: The Compute Pressure CPU Monitor leverages the W3C Compute Pressure API to report real-time CPU utilization pressure states: nominal, fair, serious, and critical. It enables developers and power users to inspect whether system hardware is operating within safe thermal parameters or approaching dynamic thermal frequency throttling. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device with no server uploads.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Native W3C PressureObserver API Integration for Real-Time CPU Metrics
  * Four-Stage Thermal Pressure Classification (Nominal, Fair, Serious, Critical)
  * Real-Time Historical Pressure Timeline Chart Rendered via HTML5 Canvas
  * Optional Controlled Multi-Core Diagnostic Workload Generator
  * Complete Local Browser Execution with Zero Hardware Telemetry Uploads
- Procedure Steps:
  * Check Hardware Support: The tool automatically detects whether your browser exposes the native W3C PressureObserver interface (supported in modern Chromium desktop browsers).
  * Observe Baseline Pressure: View your system idle pressure state on the radial status gauge and real-time canvas timeline.
  * Run Diagnostic Workload: Optionally click 'Run Diagnostic Workload' to spawn a background web worker and evaluate how your system transitions across pressure states.
  * Audit Thermal Recommendations: Inspect actionable advice regarding thermal dissipation, ventilation, and background process management.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is the W3C Compute Pressure API?
    A: The Compute Pressure API is an open W3C web standard that exposes high-level CPU pressure states (nominal, fair, serious, critical) to web applications. It allows web applications to dynamically balance compute workloads (such as video rendering, 3D graphics, or gaming) before thermal throttling causes frame stutter [Confirmed: W3C Compute Pressure Specification].
  * Q: Which browsers support the Compute Pressure API?
    A: The API is supported natively in Chromium desktop browsers including Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge version 115 and newer. In browsers without native support (such as Safari and Firefox), ToolkitGen provides simulated hardware workload profiles.
  * Q: Does this tool upload my system performance data to external servers?
    A: No. All telemetry readings, PressureObserver events, and diagnostic workload calculations execute entirely in client-side RAM inside your browser. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device.

### Gyroscope & Accelerometer Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/device_motion_logger
- Summary: The Definitive Guide to Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs): Physics, Fusion, and Applications We live in an era defined by spatial awareness.
- Overview: Gyroscope & Accelerometer Test is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Gyroscope & Accelerometer Test directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is the Z-axis $9.8$ while the phone is sitting still?
    A: This is the Gravitational Constant ($1g$). Even though your phone isn't "moving" through space, the internal MEMS sensors are constantly being pulled toward the Earth's center by gravity. This constant force of $9.81 m/s^2$ is what allows your phone to know which way is "Down" and automatically rotate your photos and videos.
  * Q: Does this work on iPhone and Android?
    A: Yes. However, Apple (iOS 13+) requires a "Secure Context" (HTTPS) and an explicit User Gesture to enable these sensors. This is why you must click the "Enable IMU Access" button on iOS. On Android, most modern browsers will work immediately, but we recommend using Chrome for the highest sampling frequency (up to 60Hz).
  * Q: What is the difference between "Alpha," "Beta," and "Gamma"?
    A: These are the Euler Angles for rotational velocity. Alpha ($\alpha$) measures rotation around the Z-axis (Compass heading/Yaw). Beta ($\beta$) measures front-to-back rotation (Pitch). Gamma ($\gamma$) measures side-to-side rotation (Roll). These three signals allow the phone to map any complex 3D rotation with 0.01-degree precision.

### USB-C Power Delivery Sniffer & Protocol Simulator
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/usb_c_pd_negotiator_sniffer
- Summary: Inspect USB-C Power Delivery contracts, VBUS voltages, and packet logs in your browser using Web Serial analyzer hardware or an interactive protocol simulator.
- Overview: Inspect USB-C Power Delivery contracts, power data objects (PDOs), and VBUS negotiation packets directly in your browser. Connect compatible Web Serial hardware analyzers or test power profiles interactively in simulated protocol mode.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Choose Mode: Select Live Web Serial Hardware mode if you have a serial protocol analyzer, or choose Interactive Protocol Simulator mode to test power profiles.
  * Connect Serial Analyzer: In hardware mode, click Connect Serial Device and select your USB-C analyzer COM port at 115200 baud.
  * Audit Power Data Objects (PDOs): Inspect Source Capabilities advertisements, Fixed Supply voltages (5V, 9V, 15V, 20V), and PPS (Programmable Power Supply) step increments.
  * Inspect Contract Logs: Verify Request packets, Accept acknowledgments, and PS_RDY transitions to ensure compliant power negotiation.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can a browser sniff USB-C Power Delivery packets without extra hardware?
    A: No. Standard computer USB controller chips do not expose raw CC-pin (Configuration Channel) BMC packets to the host operating system. To capture live PD packets, you need an external hardware analyzer (such as a Power-Z or open-source serial sniffer) connected via Web Serial.
  * Q: What is an EPR (Extended Power Range) USB-C contract?
    A: USB PD 3.1 Extended Power Range (EPR) increases maximum USB-C power delivery from 100W (20V at 5A) up to 240W (48V at 5A). EPR requires electronically marked 240W cables and specific EPR handshake negotiation.
  * Q: How do USB-C E-marker chips report cable wattage ratings?
    A: Electronically marked cables contain a small SOP' responder microchip powered by VCONN on the CC2 line. During initial discovery, the host queries the cable with a Discover Identity command, and the cable replies with maximum supported voltage and current (3A vs 5A).

### Web Serial Terminal
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/web_serial_terminal
- Summary: The Sovereign Engineer: Mastering Serial Communication in the Modern Web For decades, the serial port has been the umbilical cord of embedded engineering.
- Overview: Web Serial Terminal is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Web Serial Terminal directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why do I see squares or weird symbols in the log?
    A: This is a Baud Rate Mismatch. If your Arduino is sending data at 9600 but you have this terminal set to 115200, the "Sampling Frequency" is too high. The receiver attempts to group 1s and 0s incorrectly, resulting in nonsense Unicode characters. Always check your Serial.begin(xxxx); line in your firmware to match the selector above.
  * Q: Does this work in Firefox or Safari?
    A: Currently, no. The Web Serial API is an implementation of the Chromium engine. It is available in Chrome, Edge, and Opera. Firefox and Safari have historically resisted implementing this API due to broad "Hardware Fingerprinting" privacy concerns. We recommend using Google Chrome for all hardware-level auditing on this Canvas.
  * Q: Is my input data private when using this tool?
    A: Yes. Processing runs entirely in your local browser memory. Your inputs and configuration parameters are never uploaded to our servers.

### Web-Haptic Feedback Vibration Designer
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/haptic_rhythm_designer

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why doesn't vibration work on my iPhone/iPad?
    A: Apple's WebKit engine (used by Safari and all browsers on iOS) actively blocks the navigator.vibrate() API. This is a deliberate policy decision by Apple to prevent web ads from vibrating the phone. Currently, only Android devices and desktop computers with connected controllers support web vibration.
  * Q: How do I test my PS5 DualSense or Xbox Controller on PC?
    A: Simply connect your controller via USB or Bluetooth. Once connected, press any button on the controller to "wake" the browser's Gamepad API. This tool will automatically detect the controller (showing "Gamepad Connected") and route the vibration patterns to the controller's rumble motors instead of the device itself.
  * Q: Can I control the strength (intensity) of the vibration?
    A: On Android phones via the Web API: No. The standard API is binary (On/Off). You can simulate lower intensity by pulsing the motor rapidly (e.g., 10ms on, 10ms off), but you cannot set the voltage directly. On Gamepads: Yes. The Gamepad API supports `weakMagnitude` and `strongMagnitude` values from 0.0 to 1.0, allowing for detailed force feedback.

### WebGPU Compute & TFLOPs Benchmark
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/webgpu_compute_flops_benchmark
- Summary: WebGPU Compute Architecture: GPGPU Shaders, FP32 TFLOPs, and Thermal Throttling Direct Answer: What is a WebGPU Compute Benchmark?
- Overview: WebGPU Compute & TFLOPs Benchmark is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch WebGPU Compute & TFLOPs Benchmark directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why are WebGPU TFLOP numbers lower than advertised manufacturer specs?
    A: Manufacturer spec sheets quote theoretical peak FP32 throughput assuming 100% compute unit saturation running native Vulkan/DirectX 12 assembly. In a web browser, security memory-bounds checking, WebGPU command buffer submission latency, and OS window compositors introduce an expected 10% to 20% overhead.
  * Q: Can WebGPU compute shaders damage my graphics card?
    A: No. Modern GPUs incorporate hardware-level thermal limits and automatic power management (DVFS) enforced by on-die thermal sensors and VBIOS firmware. If temperature thresholds are reached, the GPU automatically throttles clock speeds or fans spin up to maintain safe operating temperatures.
  * Q: How do I enable WebGPU if my browser says it is unsupported?
    A: In Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, navigate to chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu and set it to Enabled, then restart the browser. Ensure your browser is updated to version 113 or newer and your graphics card drivers are current.

This specific frequency range is often effective at masking distracting sounds like conversations, which are a major disruptor in office or study environments.
  * Q: What is the "Rank" and XP system for?

    A: The default is set to the Pomodoro Technique standard of 25 minutes. However, you can use the "Long Rest" (15m) or custom modes to suit your needs. The 25-minute mark is ideal for maintaining high Beta-wave activity without crossing into mental fatigue.

### Digital Dementia Risk Screening
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/digital_dementia_risk_test
- Summary: The Cognitive Cost of Our Connected World In an age where smartphones are virtually attached to our hands, a concerning phenomenon has emerged: digital dementia .
- Overview: Digital Dementia Risk Screening is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Digital Dementia Risk Screening directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is digital dementia?
    A: Digital dementia is a condition where excessive use of digital technology leads to cognitive decline, particularly affecting memory, attention span, and critical thinking skills. The term was coined by neuroscientist Manfred Spitzer to describe how constant digital device use can impair brain function similar to the effects of dementia.
  * Q: How does screen time affect brain health?
    A: Excessive screen time can rewire neural pathways, reduce gray matter density in areas responsible for memory and emotional regulation, impair attention span, reduce the brain's ability to form new memories, and decrease cognitive flexibility. Studies show that heavy smartphone users have reduced activity in the prefrontal cortex, the brain's decision-making center.
  * Q: Can I reverse digital dementia effects?
    A: Yes, the brain retains neuroplasticity throughout life. By reducing screen time, engaging in analog activities like reading physical books, practicing memory exercises, getting adequate sleep, and participating in social interactions, you can restore cognitive function over time.

## Category: Productivity / Utility

### Black-Scholes Options Greeks & Volatility Matrix
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/black_scholes_heatmap
- Summary: Calculate Black-Scholes European call/put pricing, Delta, Gamma, Theta, and Vega across strike and expiration surfaces with CSV volatility export.
- Overview: Calculate theoretical option prices and sensitivity Greeks (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, Rho) across a 2D volatility and expiration surface. Uses the Black-Scholes-Merton model with continuous dividend yield adjustments and exportable matrix CSV data.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Enter Asset & Strike Parameters: Input current underlying stock price ($S$), option strike price ($K$), days to expiration ($T$), and annual risk-free rate ($r$).
  * Adjust Implied Volatility: Set implied volatility ($\\sigma$) and continuous dividend yield ($q$) to match real-time market options chain pricing.
  * Toggle Greek Sensitivity Surfaces: Switch between Option Price, Delta, Gamma, Theta (daily decay), and Vega heatmaps to visualize risk exposure across price intervals.
  * Export Surface Matrix: Export the complete calculated Greek matrix to a CSV file for financial modeling in Excel or Python.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What are the limitations of the Black-Scholes model in modern markets?
    A: Black-Scholes assumes constant volatility, constant interest rates, log-normal asset price distributions, and European exercise (no early exercise). Real-world markets exhibit volatility smiles/skews, fat-tailed returns, and American-style early exercise risk.
  * Q: What does Option Theta measure?
    A: Theta (\Theta) quantifies the rate of decline in the option's value with the passage of time (time decay), expressed in dollars per share per calendar day. Theta accelerates exponentially in the final 30 days before expiration for at-the-money options.
  * Q: How does dividend yield affect European Call and Put prices?
    A: Dividends decrease the future expected price of the underlying stock. A higher continuous dividend yield ($q$) lowers call prices and increases put prices.

### LLM Prompt Engineering Builder
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/prompt_template_builder
- Summary: Large Language Model (LLM) , where the quality of your career, business, and education is increasingly dictated by the quality of your instructions.
- Overview: LLM Prompt Engineering Builder is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.

- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch LLM Prompt Engineering Builder directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Does a longer prompt always mean a better result?
    A: No. There is a concept called "Attention Dilution." Large models have a limited attention span (context window). If you fill a prompt with 2,000 words of unnecessary fluff, the AI might lose focus on the primary "Task." The goal of our Prompt Architect is to increase Density and Clarity, not length. A 200-word structured prompt is almost always superior to a 2,000-word conversational story.
  * Q: What is "Temperature" in AI and why does it matter?
    A: Temperature is a setting that controls the Creativity vs. Factuality of the model's predictions. A temperature of 0.1 is very "cold" and literal—perfect for coding or data analysis. A temperature of 0.8 is "hot" and creative—perfect for storytelling. While you can't set temperature in our prompt builder (it's a setting in the AI interface), your choice of "Role" and "Format" effectively signals the model to behave with a specific temperature-like consistency.
  * Q: Can I use this for programming and code refactoring?
    A: Yes, it is highly recommended. When prompting for code, use the RTF Model. Set the Role to "Expert [Language] Developer," the Task to "Refactor this code for readability and performance," and the Format to "Clean Code Block with inline comments." Providing the context of your existing codebase is the best way to get production-ready suggestions.

  * Q: What is the 100x multiplier?

  * Q: Is webcam HRV measurement accurate?
    A: Webcam-based HRV using rPPG provides estimates within reasonable accuracy for wellness purposes. Studies show correlation coefficients of 0.85-0.95 compared to chest-strap monitors.   * Q: How long does it take to improve HRV?
    A: Many users notice improved HRV scores within 2-4 weeks of consistent daily practice. The key is consistency—short daily sessions outperform occasional long ones.
  * Q: What is a good RMSSD score?
    A: RMSSD varies significantly by age, fitness level, and measurement conditions. Generally, RMSSD above 50ms indicates good parasympathetic function. Athletes often have values above 80ms, while chronically stressed individuals may have scores below 30ms. Focus on your personal trend rather than absolute numbers—improvement over time is the key metric.

## Category: Developer / Security

### C2PA Content Credentials Viewer
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/c2pa_metadata_viewer
- Summary: Inspect C2PA Content Credentials, verify cryptographic provenance manifests, and detect AI-generated image source assertions locally.
- Overview: The C2PA Content Credentials Viewer inspects JPEG, PNG, WebP, and AVIF media files for embedded Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) manifests. It parses JPEG Universal Metadata Box Format (JUMBF) containers in browser memory to reveal the issuing signing authority, software claim generator (Adobe Photoshop, DALL-E, Midjourney, Leica), editing history, and AI source classifications. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device with no server uploads.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Client-Side JUMBF Box Binary Parser (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, and MP4 Media)
  * AI-Generated Media Detection (trainedAlgorithmicMedia and Composite Assertions)
  * Cryptographic Signing Organization and X.509 Certificate Chain Inspection
  * Asset Modification History Timeline (Created, Cropped, Color Corrected, Composited)
  * Complete Local RAM Execution with Zero Image Cloud Telemetry
- Procedure Steps:
  * Select or Drop Media File: Drag and drop any JPEG, PNG, WebP, or AVIF image into the local inspection zone.
  * Parse Provenance Manifest: The tool automatically scans binary markers (APP11 JUMBF, caIp, or C2PA chunks) in client memory.
  * Verify AI Source Assertions: Check whether the image was flagged as AI generated (e.g. via DALL-E, Midjourney, or Adobe Firefly) or captured with a hardware camera.
  * Review Editing Actions: Examine the recorded historical actions applied to the digital asset throughout its production lifecycle.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is C2PA and Content Credentials?
    A: C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) is an open technical standard developed by Adobe, Microsoft, Intel, and the BBC. It embeds tamper-evident cryptographic manifests into media files, recording who created the file, what software generated or modified it, and whether artificial intelligence was used [Confirmed: C2PA Technical Specifications].
  * Q: How does C2PA detect AI-generated imagery?
    A: AI generators that adhere to C2PA standards (such as OpenAI DALL-E 3, Midjourney, and Adobe Firefly) sign an assertion called digitalSourceType set to 'trainedAlgorithmicMedia' or 'compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia'. This assertion is cryptographically sealed into the file manifest.
  * Q: Can C2PA metadata be stripped from an image?
    A: Yes. If an image is screenshotted, re-compressed through social media apps (Twitter/X, Facebook) that strip metadata, or converted via basic image converters, the C2PA container is discarded. However, any modification to a C2PA-bearing image without re-signing breaks cryptographic hash validation, immediately flagging the manifest as modified.

### X.509 Certificate Decoder & Validator
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/x509_certificate_decoder
- Summary: Decode PEM and DER SSL/TLS X.509 certificates locally. Inspect SANs, validity expiration, ASN.1 structures, and calculate SHA-256 fingerprints.
- Overview: The X.509 Certificate Decoder parses PEM and DER encoded SSL/TLS certificates directly inside browser memory. It extracts the Subject, Issuer, Subject Alternative Names (SANs), Serial Number, validity dates, key algorithm, and calculates SHA-256 and SHA-1 fingerprints without transmitting cryptographic material over the network. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device with no server uploads.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Client-Side ASN.1 DER Tag-Length-Value (TLV) Binary Parser
  * Subject Alternative Name (SANs) and Wildcard Domain Inspector
  * Real-Time Expiration Countdown and Validity Status Alert
  * Cryptographic SHA-256 and SHA-1 Fingerprint Hashes with One-Click Copy
  * Complete Local RAM Execution with No Server Uploads
- Procedure Steps:
  * Paste or Upload Certificate: Paste your PEM certificate block (beginning with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----) or upload a .crt, .pem, or .cer file.
  * Decode ASN.1 Hierarchy: Click 'Decode Certificate' or select 'Load Sample' to parse the cryptographic structure in client RAM.
  * Inspect Subject and SANs: Review verified hostnames, wildcards, issuer authority, and key specifications.
  * Verify Expiration and Fingerprints: Check remaining days until certificate renewal and copy SHA-256 verification fingerprints.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is an X.509 certificate?
    A: An X.509 certificate is a digital cryptographic document standardized under RFC 5280. It binds an identity (such as a website domain or organization) to a public encryption key using a digital signature from a trusted Certificate Authority [Confirmed: RFC 5280 Specifications].
  * Q: Why are Subject Alternative Names (SANs) preferred over Common Name (CN)?
    A: Modern browsers and TLS clients deprecate reliance on the Subject Common Name (CN) field due to ambiguity and lack of multi-domain support. RFC 6125 mandates that hostname validation rely exclusively on the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) extension [Confirmed: RFC 6125].
  * Q: Are my private keys exposed if I decode a certificate here?
    A: No. An X.509 public certificate contains only the public key and identity metadata; it never contains the private key. Furthermore, this tool processes all parsing locally in browser RAM without server transmission.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is my printed black "Rich Black"?
    A: "Rich Black" is a mixture of 100% Key (Black) plus a percentage of Cyan, Magenta, and Yellow (often 60/40/40). This creates a deeper, darker black than using just 100% K, which can sometimes look like dark charcoal grey on absorbent paper.
  * Q: What is the difference between coated and uncoated paper?
    A: Coated paper has a clay layer that keeps ink on the surface, resulting in sharper images and vibrant colors. Uncoated paper acts like a sponge, absorbing ink, which causes "dot gain" (dots spreading) and generally results in darker, more muted colors.
  * Q: Is my input data private when using this tool?
    A: Yes. Processing runs entirely in your local browser memory. Your inputs and configuration parameters are never uploaded to our servers.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Does measuring with a credit card really work?
    A: Yes. Credit cards (ID-1 format) are standardized globally to exactly 85.60mm × 53.98mm. By resizing the on-screen box to match your physical card, the browser can calculate the exact pixel density of your specific screen, allowing for millimetre-perfect rendering of the watch graphics.
  * Q: Can I wear a 44mm watch on a 6-inch wrist?
    A: Physically, yes, but aesthetically, it may look oversized ("the frying pan effect"). A 6-inch wrist generally supports a lug-to-lug distance of roughly 44-46mm maximum. Most 44mm diameter watches have a lug-to-lug of 50mm+, which would overhang your wrist.
  * Q: What is the "Lug-to-Lug" multiplier?
    A: While not exact, a common estimation is that the lug-to-lug distance is roughly 1.25x to 1.3x the case diameter for standard watches. For example, a 40mm watch typically spans 48mm to 50mm lug-to-lug.

    A: No, the images are not live video feeds. They are composites of cloud-free photographs taken by satellites over the last 1-3 years. This ensures you get a clear view of the terrain without weather obstruction.
  * Q: Why can't I see street names?
    A: The game specifically uses "Satellite Only" tiles (provided by Esri World Imagery) to strip away political labels. The goal is to identify locations based on physical geography and human footprint, not by reading text.
  * Q: How many locations are in the game?
    A: The database currently rotates through 25 iconic high-resolution locations, ranging from famous monuments like the Taj Mahal to natural wonders like the Grand Canyon. We regularly update the coordinate list to keep the challenge fresh.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is usable console SSD space lower than advertised capacity?
    A: Drive manufacturers market capacity using decimal gigabytes (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes), whereas console operating systems compute binary gibibytes (1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes). Furthermore, console operating systems reserve between 110 GB and 198 GB for system software, firmware rollback partitions, scratchpad caching, and recording buffers.
  * Q: What is the actual usable capacity of a PlayStation 5 SSD?
    A: The original PlayStation 5 (825 GB SSD) provides approximately 667.2 GB of usable storage [Confirmed: Sony Interactive Entertainment, Nov 2020]. The PS5 Slim (1 TB SSD) offers approximately 848 GB [Confirmed: Sony Interactive Entertainment, Nov 2023]. The PS5 Pro (2 TB SSD) provides approximately 1.89 TB of usable space [Confirmed: Sony Interactive Entertainment, Nov 2024].
  * Q: What is the usable capacity on Xbox Series X and Series S?
    A: The Xbox Series X (1 TB internal drive) offers approximately 802 GB of usable space [Confirmed: Microsoft Xbox Wire, Nov 2020]. The Xbox Series S 512 GB model provides approximately 364 GB usable space, while the 1 TB Series S provides approximately 802 GB usable space [Confirmed: Microsoft Xbox Wire, Sep 2023].

### Frame Rate Judder & Pacing Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/framerate_judder_pacing_test
- Summary: Benchmark display motion judder and frame pacing: test 30 FPS vs 40 FPS vs 60 FPS raster sweeps, detect 120Hz refresh rates, calculate cadence dividers, and diagnose OLED stutter.
- Overview: The Frame Rate Judder & Pacing Test benchmarks your monitor or television for motion smoothness, display cadence dividers, and sample-and-hold OLED stutter. It features an interactive quad-cadence raster motion sweep comparing 30 FPS, 40 FPS, 60 FPS, and native display refresh rates in real time, a high-precision browser refresh rate detector, and a display cadence calculator illustrating why 40 FPS modes require a 120Hz container ($120 / 40 = 3$). All telemetry executes locally in browser memory.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Real-Time Quad-Cadence Motion Sweep (30 FPS, 40 FPS, 60 FPS, and Native Refresh)
  * Sub-Millisecond Browser Refresh Rate and Frame Delta Jitter Telemetry
  * Display Cadence Divider Calculator (Integer Ratios vs 3:2 Pulldown Judder)
  * HDMI 2.1 VRR 48Hz Hardware Floor and LFC (Low Framerate Compensation) Evaluator
  * OLED Sample-and-Hold Retinal Stutter versus Motion Blur Visualizer
  * Console and Television Display Calibration Troubleshooting Checklist
- Procedure Steps:
  * Connect Your Gaming Display: Open this diagnostic on your PC, laptop, or console browser connected to your gaming monitor or television.
  * Observe Quad-Cadence Motion Bars: Track the moving raster bars with your eyes. Compare the perceived stepping and jitter between 30 FPS, 40 FPS, 60 FPS, and native display refresh.
  * Check Hardware Telemetry: Inspect the live FPS and frame-time delta metrics to verify whether your operating system and browser deliver true 60Hz or 120Hz pacing.
  * Calculate Display Cadence Dividers: Select your game target frame rate and display refresh rate in the cadence calculator to see if the frame times divide evenly or induce pulldown judder.
  * Evaluate VRR and LFC Boundaries: Toggle the VRR option to inspect whether your target framerate falls inside the native 48Hz-120Hz window or triggers Low Framerate Compensation.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why does 30 FPS look choppy on OLED televisions compared to older LCDs?
    A: OLED pixels possess near-instantaneous response times (under 0.1 ms GtG), whereas older LCD panels exhibited 5 to 15 ms of liquid crystal transition blur. On sample-and-hold OLED displays, each 30 FPS frame remains completely static for 33.3 milliseconds before instantly stepping to the next position. Because your retina tracks continuous motion across the screen, this instant stepping creates high-contrast retinal judder. The older LCD panel's slow response time created natural motion blur that masked this stepping [Confirmed: Blur Busters, DisplayMate].
  * Q: Why do 40 FPS console modes require a 120Hz display?
    A: On a standard 60Hz display, 40 FPS does not divide evenly: 60 divided by 40 equals 1.5 display refreshes per frame. The television must alternate between holding a frame for 1 refresh (16.67 ms) and 2 refreshes (33.33 ms), creating severe rhythmic 3:2 judder. On a 120Hz display, 120 divided by 40 equals exactly 3.0 refreshes per frame. Every frame is displayed for precisely 25.0 milliseconds in an even 1:1:1 integer cadence, eliminating judder while saving ~33% GPU render budget compared to 60 FPS [Confirmed: Sony Interactive Entertainment, Digital Foundry].
  * Q: What is the HDMI 2.1 VRR 48Hz floor and what is LFC?
    A: Standard HDMI 2.1 Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) modules operate within a hardware frequency window of 48 Hz to 120 Hz. When a game's frame rate drops below 48 FPS (such as a 30 FPS title), the display cannot match the frame rate 1:1. The console and display engage Low Framerate Compensation (LFC), which multiplies frames (e.g. duplicating 30 FPS frames twice to refresh at 60 Hz). On OLED televisions, rapid transitions across the 48Hz boundary can cause slight gamma luminance shifts perceived as near-black flicker.

### Frame Time Calculator
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/frame_time_calculator
- Summary: Convert frame rates to frame times, calculate frame budget tolerances, and evaluate 1% low and 0.1% low pacing stability.
- Overview: The Frame Time Calculator converts frames per second (FPS) into exact millisecond frame presentation budgets and analyzes pasted benchmark datasets to compute 1% low and 0.1% low frame rates, pacing consistency, and micro-stutter frequency. Unlike simple average FPS, frame time variance exposes transient stutter and inconsistent frame delivery. All analysis executes locally in browser memory.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Bi-Directional FPS and Frame Time (ms) Conversion
  * Standard Refresh Rate Budget Verification (30, 60, 120, 144, 240 Hz)
  * Percentile Pacing Analysis (1% Low and 0.1% Low FPS)
  * Frame Time Variance and Micro-Stutter Detection Graph
- Procedure Steps:
  * Quick Conversion: Enter any target frame rate or millisecond interval to calculate reciprocal frame delivery budgets.
  * Paste Benchmark Telemetry: Paste raw frame times (ms) or frame rates from CapFrameX, PresentMon, or game engine logs.
  * Run Pacing Analysis: Click Calculate Statistics to process frame percentiles and view the visual frame delivery graph.
  * Evaluate Frame Pacing: Review your 1% low FPS, standard deviation, and micro-stutter count against target display budgets.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is frame time more informative than average FPS?
    A: Average FPS obscures brief, severe pauses. If a game renders 59 frames in 500 milliseconds and spends 500 milliseconds stuck on a single frame, the average frame rate still appears as 60 FPS, even though the user experiences a jarring half-second freeze. Frame time graphs reveal the exact duration of each rendered frame.
  * Q: What do 1% Low and 0.1% Low metrics mean?
    A: The 1% Low represents the 99th percentile slowest frame times in a benchmark dataset, converted to an equivalent frame rate. The 0.1% Low captures the single worst 0.1% of stutter frames (the 99.9th percentile). When 1% lows diverge substantially from the average FPS, perceptible stuttering and pacing instability are present.
  * Q: What is the frame budget for a 60 FPS game?
    A: At 60 FPS, the GPU and CPU pipeline must render and present each frame in exactly 16.67 milliseconds (1,000ms / 60). At 120 FPS, the budget shrinks to 8.33 milliseconds.

### Game Download Time Calculator
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/game_download_time_calculator
- Summary: Calculate download duration, transfer rates, and ISP data allowance impact for console and PC games based on bandwidth and network overhead.
- Overview: The Game Download Time Calculator computes realistic download durations for game installations based on package size and broadband throughput. By factoring in network protocol overhead, TCP window scaling, and content delivery network routing, it provides both ideal and real-world estimates along with monthly data cap consumption. All calculations execute locally in your browser.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Ideal and Real-World Transfer Estimates
  * TCP/IP Protocol Overhead Compensation
  * Common Game Size and Bandwidth Presets
  * Monthly Data Cap Usage Modeling
- Procedure Steps:
  * Enter Game Size: Input the total installation or patch size in gigabytes (GB) or select a standard preset.
  * Specify Download Speed: Enter your broadband connection speed in megabits per second (Mbps).
  * Adjust Overhead Buffer: Set the estimated network protocol and storage write overhead (standard baseline is 10%).
  * Review Results: Inspect total transfer duration, effective transfer rate in megabytes per second (MB/s), and data allowance impact.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is my real download speed slower than my internet plan?
    A: Internet service plans are marketed in megabits per second (Mbps), while files are measured in bytes (1 byte = 8 bits). Furthermore, transport protocol headers (TCP/IP), TLS encryption handshakes, local disk write buffers, and server-side CDN rate limiting typically consume 8% to 15% of nominal throughput.
  * Q: How does a game patch or delta update affect download time?
    A: Modern distribution platforms frequently distribute compressed delta patches rather than full base games. While a patch download may be smaller, local console or PC installation involves uncompressing and patching existing package archives, which can extend total time beyond the raw network transfer period.
  * Q: What network overhead percentage is standard for residential broadband?
    A: A conservative buffer of 10% to 12% accurately reflects protocol encapsulation and packet retransmission on wired Ethernet. Over Wi-Fi connections with physical wall attenuation or channel interference, effective overhead often reaches 15% to 20%.

### Gamepad Button & Input Tester

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is my controller not detected when I plug it in?
    A: Browsers enforce a security policy requiring a physical button press on the gamepad before exposing device input events to JavaScript. Connect the controller and press any button (such as A, Cross, or D-Pad) to activate detection.
  * Q: Which controllers are supported?
    A: Any controller recognized by your operating system as an XInput, DirectInput, or HID gamepad is supported, including PlayStation DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox Wireless Controllers, Nintendo Switch Pro Controllers, and third-party fightsticks.
  * Q: What is controller polling rate?
    A: Polling rate is the frequency (measured in Hertz, or Hz) at which the controller transmits updated button and stick states to the host system. Standard Bluetooth connections typically poll between 125 Hz (8ms) and 250 Hz (4ms), while high-performance wired USB controllers can poll at 500 Hz to 1,000 Hz (1ms).

### Gamepad Drift & Input Diagnostic Suite

All diagnostics execute locally in your browser memory.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Universal Gamepad API Polling Engine with Optional Chromium WebHID Inspection
  * Dual-Axis Analog Stick Oscilloscopes with Persistent Coordinate Tracing
  * Real-Time Unit-Circle Circularity Error and Square-Gating Detection
  * Centering Jitter and Electrical Noise Analysis with Deadzone Tuning Suggestions
  * Analog Trigger Pressure Resolution and Button Chatter Detection
  * Exportable Hardware Warranty and RMA Diagnostic Scorecard
- Procedure Steps:
  * Connect Your Controller: Connect your PlayStation DualSense, Xbox Wireless Controller, Switch Pro Controller, or third-party gamepad via USB or Bluetooth.
  * Initialize Input: Press any face button (A, X, or Cross) to permit browser access to the Gamepad API.
  * Test Centering & Resting Drift: Release both analog sticks and observe the centering crosshair to see if resting coordinates drift beyond the 0.05 threshold.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why does my controller not appear immediately upon connecting?
    A: Modern web browsers enforce an explicit security protocol: the Gamepad API remains idle until the user interacts with the controller. Pressing any button (A, Cross, or Trigger) grants permission to stream telemetry.
  * Q: What is an acceptable circularity error score?
    A: For factory PlayStation DualSense and Xbox Wireless controllers using potentiometer sensors, circularity errors between 8% and 15% are standard due to mechanical square-gating. High-end Hall Effect controllers (e.g., GuliKit, 8BitDo) typically achieve circularity errors under 2% to 4%.
  * Q: How does potentiometer wear cause stick drift?
    A: Potentiometers utilize a physical metal wiper sliding across a resistive carbon film track. Over hundreds of hours, mechanical friction wears away the carbon layer, generating carbon dust and erratic contact resistance that the operating system interprets as phantom stick movement [Confirmed: Hardware teardown analysis].

### HDR & OLED Calibration Patterns
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/hdr_display_calibration_patterns
- Summary: Generate high-precision display test patterns: detect 8-bit FRC color banding, test 5% near-black OLED panel uniformity, and check Mini-LED blooming.
- Overview: The HDR and OLED Calibration Patterns generator produces browser-calibrated test patterns for evaluating television and monitor image fidelity. It includes a 10-bit smooth grayscale gradient sweep to detect FRC dithering and color banding, a 5% near-black OLED gray field to identify dirty screen effect (DSE) and vignetting, a Mini-LED blooming starfield, and peak white clipping patterns for HGiG setup. All patterns render locally in client memory.
- Key Capabilities:
  * 10-Bit and 12-Bit Smooth Grayscale Gradient Sweep to Expose 8-Bit FRC Banding
  * 5% Near-Black OLED Uniformity Field to Inspect Vertical Banding and Vignetting
  * High-Contrast Mini-LED Blooming Starfield Test Pattern for Local Dimming Zones
  * Stepped Peak White Highlight Clipping Blocks (1000 Nits, 2000 Nits, 4000 Nits)
  * One-Click Fullscreen Canvas Inspection with Dark Room Ambient Interface
- Procedure Steps:
  * Dim Ambient Room Lighting: For accurate near-black OLED and Mini-LED blooming evaluation, perform testing in a darkened room without direct screen reflections.
  * Select Test Pattern: Choose from the Grayscale Gradient, 5% Near-Black Field, Starfield Blooming, or Peak Highlight Clipping.
  * Activate Fullscreen Mode: Click Fullscreen to expand the pattern to the physical edges of your display panel, hiding browser UI elements.
  * Audit Display Uniformity: Inspect the panel for visible vertical stripes, color tinting across corners, or haloing around high-contrast star elements.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What causes color banding on modern gaming monitors and TVs?
    A: Color banding occurs when a display cannot render subtle tonal transitions smoothly. Panels with 8-bit color depth only have 256 shades per RGB channel (16.7 million total colors). When rendering high-dynamic-range content without spatial/temporal dithering (FRC), visible stair-stepping artifacts appear across gradients.
  * Q: What is the 5% gray test and why is it standard for OLEDs?
    A: OLED subpixels produce perfect zero-nit blacks when turned off. However, transitioning subpixels from pure black to just above black (1% to 5% luminance) is where manufacturing variations in thin-film transistors (TFTs) become visible, manifesting as subtle vertical stripes or panel vignetting.
  * Q: How does Mini-LED blooming occur?
    A: Mini-LED displays use localized full-array backlights divided into hundreds or thousands of physical dimming zones. When a small bright object (such as a star in space or white text) appears against a deep black background, light spills into adjacent pixels within the same dimming zone, creating a noticeable halo or 'blooming' effect.

### Slow-Motion Video Input Lag Meter
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/slowmo_latency_meter
- Summary: Measure end-to-end display latency and controller input lag using smartphone slow-motion video recordings with frame-by-frame timestamp analysis.
- Overview: The Slow-Motion Video Input Lag Meter turns any modern smartphone camera into an optical latency testing tool. By stepping frame-by-frame through a 120fps or 240fps slow-motion recording of your physical finger actuating a button and the screen reacting, it calculates exact end-to-end system input latency in milliseconds with jitter confidence bounds. All video decoding occurs locally in browser memory without server uploads.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local In-Memory Video Processing (Zero Cloud Uploads for Complete Privacy)
  * Frame-Accurate Stepping Engine Supporting 120fps, 240fps, 480fps, and 960fps
  * Two-Point Visual Timestamp Marking: Mechanical Actuation to First Pixel Shift
  * Sub-Millisecond System Latency Calculation with Rolling Shutter Jitter Intervals
  * Standardized Optical Diagnostic Report Export for Gaming Communities
- Procedure Steps:
  * Record Your Test Video: Record a slow-motion video (120fps or 240fps) on your smartphone showing both your controller/mouse button and the screen in the same frame.
  * Load Video Locally: Drag and drop the video file into the browser workspace. The file processes entirely within local RAM.
  * Select Recording Frame Rate: Confirm your smartphone's slow-motion framerate (typically 120fps or 240fps on modern iOS and Android devices).
  * Mark the Button Contact Frame: Use the frame stepper buttons to pause on the exact frame where your finger initiates physical contact.
  * Mark the Pixel Reaction Frame: Step forward until the first pixel change (gunfire, jump, cursor movement) appears on the display panel.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: How accurate is testing input lag with a smartphone slow-motion camera?
    A: Extremely accurate when calibrated properly. At 240 frames per second, each individual frame represents exactly 4.17 milliseconds of real-world elapsed time (1,000 ms / 240 fps). The resulting measurement error is bounded by ±2.08 ms, which rivals multi-thousand-dollar hardware oscilloscope setups [Confirmed: Optical latency testing methodologies].
  * Q: Does my video file get uploaded to ToolkitGen servers?
    A: No. All video decoding, playback, and canvas frame grabbing execute locally in your browser memory using HTML5 Video and browser memory object URLs. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device.
  * Q: What is the difference between button-to-pixel lag and button-to-USB lag?
    A: Button-to-USB latency only measures peripheral switch scan time (typically 1ms to 8ms). Button-to-pixel (total system latency) measures the full pipeline: peripheral debounce + USB transmission + game engine render tick + GPU queue + video cable transmission + display panel scanout.

### TV & Gaming Display Capability Checker
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/tv_gaming_capability_checker
- Summary: Test television and monitor gaming capabilities: detect real-time 60Hz and 120Hz refresh rates, inspect HDR dynamic range, verify HDMI 2.1 bandwidth, and calibrate HGiG game settings.
- Overview: The TV and Gaming Display Capability Checker audits your connected television or monitor for 120Hz refresh rates, HDR color spaces (Display P3 / Rec.2020), and Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) readiness. It features a real-time requestAnimationFrame delta sampler, an HDMI 2.1 bandwidth calculator, a judder and tear simulation pattern, and an optimal TV picture mode calibration checklist for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles. All diagnostics execute locally in your browser.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Real-Time Hardware Refresh Rate and Frame Delta Monitor (60Hz, 120Hz, 144Hz, 240Hz)
  * High Dynamic Range (HDR) and Wide Color Gamut (Display P3) Media Query Auditing
  * Interactive HDMI 2.1 Video Bandwidth and Chroma Subsampling Calculator
  * Interactive Judder, Micro-Stutter, and VRR Raster Simulation Pattern
  * Console and Television Calibration Checklist (HGiG, Game Optimizer, ALLM, RGB Range)
- Procedure Steps:
  * Connect Your Gaming Display: Connect your PC, laptop, or console browser to your television or gaming monitor via HDMI or DisplayPort.
  * Audit Refresh Rate and Frame Stability: Observe the live FPS telemetry counter to confirm if your panel is delivering native 60Hz, 120Hz, or higher frame pacing.
  * Check HDR and Color Space: Review the automated browser dynamic range and Display P3 wide color gamut status cards.
  * Test for Judder and Tearing: Activate the moving raster bar test pattern to identify micro-stutters, frame pacing drops, or visual tearing.
  * Follow the HDMI 2.1 Calibration Guide: Configure your television picture settings using the step-by-step checklist to enable HGiG tone mapping and low-latency Game Mode.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is my 120Hz television showing 60Hz in the browser?
    A: Several factors can cap browser refresh rates at 60Hz: (1) Windows or macOS display settings may be defaulted to 60Hz; (2) The connected HDMI cable or port may be limited to HDMI 2.0; (3) The television input label may not have 'Enhanced Format' or 'Ultra Deep Color' enabled; (4) The browser hardware acceleration setting may be disabled.
  * Q: What is the difference between HDMI 2.0 and HDMI 2.1?
    A: HDMI 2.0 is capped at 18.0 Gbps (TMDS), which permits uncompressed 4K at 60Hz with 8-bit color. HDMI 2.1 expands bandwidth up to 40.0 Gbps (on PS5) and 48.0 Gbps (on Xbox Series X and modern GPUs), enabling uncompressed 4K at 120Hz with 10-bit HDR and Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) simultaneously [Confirmed: HDMI Forum].
  * Q: What is HGiG and why is it recommended over TV Dynamic Tone Mapping?
    A: HGiG (HDR Gaming Interest Group) turns off the television's internal dynamic tone mapping algorithm. This allows the console itself to perform tone mapping directly to the display's exact peak luminance clipping point (e.g., 800 nits on OLED). If both the TV Dynamic Tone Mapping and console HDR are enabled, 'double tone mapping' occurs, blowing out specular highlights.

### TV Game Mode & Input Lag Tester
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/tv_game_mode_input_lag_tester
- Summary: Benchmark perceived display latency, verify 60Hz and 120Hz frame pacing, and calibrate television Game Mode and ALLM settings.
- Overview: The TV Game Mode and Input Lag Tester provides a client-side visual stimulus loop to measure end-to-end response time and display latency across television panels and external monitors. It features an interactive refresh rate verification loop, statistical latency aggregation (mean, minimum, and standard deviation), and a comprehensive television picture-processing calibration guide for ALLM and VRR. All testing runs locally in browser memory.
- Key Capabilities:
  * High-Precision Hardware Timer Reaction Loop
  * Real-Time Browser Refresh Rate and Frame Pacing Monitor
  * Multi-Trial Latency Statistics (Mean, Min, Max, StdDev)
  * ALLM, VRR, and TV Post-Processing Calibration Guide
- Procedure Steps:
  * Prepare Your Display: Connect your PC or console to your television via HDMI. Ensure Game Mode is enabled in your TV picture settings.
  * Start Latency Test: Click the Start Benchmark button. Watch the stage canvas for the rapid color shift.
  * Press Key on Flash: Press the Spacebar or click the mouse immediately when the stimulus card turns green.
  * Review Latency Stats: Complete 5 trials to generate your mean response time, standard deviation, and responsiveness rating.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is the difference between input lag and pixel response time?
    A: Input lag is the total delay between sending an electrical command (such as pressing a button) and the resulting action appearing on screen. Pixel response time (GtG) is merely the duration required for physical liquid crystal molecules or OLED subpixels to transition between colors. A television can have fast 1ms pixel response time but high 80ms input lag if post-processing is active.
  * Q: How does TV Game Mode reduce input lag?
    A: Standard television picture modes route incoming HDMI video through internal digital signal processors (DSPs) to apply noise reduction, motion smoothing (frame interpolation), dynamic contrast, and upscaling. Game Mode bypasses these processing pipelines, cutting input latency from 60ms-120ms down to under 10ms-15ms.
  * Q: What is Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM)?
    A: ALLM is an HDMI 2.1 protocol feature that enables a connected console or PC to automatically command the television display to switch into low-latency Game Mode upon launching a game, and revert to normal picture mode when playing a movie.

## Category: Display / Screen

### Backlight Bleed Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/monitor_backlight_bleed
- Summary: Most modern LCDs—including IPS, VA, and TN panels—rely on a background lighting array that must be filtered through layers of liquid crystals and polarizers.
- Overview: Backlight Bleed Test is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Backlight Bleed Test directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can software "fix" backlight bleed?
    A: No. Backlight bleed is a physical hardware defect involving the panel layers and the frame. No software update or color calibration can remove it. You can only "Hide" it by lowering the monitor's global brightness or using bias lighting (LED strips behind the monitor) to reduce the perceived contrast between the bleed and the room.
  * Q: Does this work on Android or Tablet screens?
    A: Absolutely. Many modern tablets and high-end Android phones use IPS or OLED displays. This tool is fully responsive. On Android, open this page in Chrome, tap the "Execute Pure Void" button, and the browser will automatically enter fullscreen mode to cover the entire panel, allowing you to check for manufacturing defects on your mobile device.
  * Q: What is "Clouding"?
    A: Clouding is a form of Mura (Japanese for unevenness). It looks like blurry clouds of light in the middle of a dark screen. It is usually caused by the physical pressure of internal components against the liquid crystal layer. If your monitor shows heavy clouding in our black screen test, it may have been damaged or warped during shipping.

  * Q: Why do older people have lower CFF?
    A: Neural processing slows with age. The retinal ganglion cells and subsequent neural pathways take longer to reset and fire again. Additionally, the crystalline lens yellows with age, reducing light transmission to the retina.
  * Q: Can I improve my CFF?

### Dead Pixel Checker
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/dead_pixel_check

  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can a dead pixel spread to other pixels?
    A: Generally, no. A dead pixel is a localized hardware failure in the TFT backplane. It is not a "contagious" defect. However, if a cluster of dead pixels appears, it may indicate a larger problem with the display controller or physical damage (like pressure) to that specific area of the panel.
  * Q: Will a screenshot show my dead pixels?
    A: No. A screenshot captures the digital signal being sent to the monitor, not the physical output of the monitor itself. If you want to prove a dead pixel for a warranty claim, you must take a physical photograph of your screen using a camera or phone.
  * Q: Does this work on mobile (Android/iPhone)?
    A: Absolutely. The Dead Pixel Detector is fully responsive. On Android and iOS, tapping the "Full Screen" button will leverage the browser's Fullscreen API to hide the URL bar and navigation, giving you a pure diagnostic field. This is the most reliable way to check a new phone for panel defects before the return period ends.

### Display Color Gamut Visualizer
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/display_color_gamut_visualizer
- Summary: Free online display gamut visualizer (srgb) with instant results. No account required. Calculations run in your browser, and inputs are not uploaded.
- Overview: Display Gamut Visualizer (sRGB) is a free online utility built for developers, designers, and professionals. It runs directly on your device using standard HTML5 APIs and WebAssembly. No signup or account is required. Calculations run locally in your browser, and your input parameters or files are not uploaded to our servers.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Display Color Gamut Visualizer directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is the difference between sRGB and DCI-P3?
    A: DCI-P3 offers approximately 25% more colors than sRGB, particularly in the red and green ranges. sRGB is the web standard used by browsers and operating systems, while DCI-P3 is used for digital cinema projection and increasingly by HDR content creators and gaming monitors.
  * Q: Do I need a wide-gamut monitor for photo editing?
    A: For web-delivered photography, a monitor with 95%+ sRGB coverage is sufficient. However, if you work with print output or need to soft-proof Adobe RGB content, a wide-gamut monitor with 90%+ Adobe RGB coverage is essential. Professional photographers often prefer wide-gamut displays with hardware calibration.
  * Q: What does "100% sRGB" actually mean?
    A: When a monitor claims "100% sRGB," it means the display can reproduce 100% of the colors within the sRGB color space triangle. However, this doesn't guarantee color accuracy (Delta E). A monitor might cover 100% of sRGB but still produce inaccurate colors. Always check Delta E specifications for true color accuracy.

### Monitor Calibration Tool
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/monitor_gamma_calibrator
- Summary: Perception: A Master Guide to Monitor Calibration and Gamma Ramps A display is a window into a digital reality, but that window is rarely clean out of the box.
- Overview: Monitor Calibration Tool is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Monitor Calibration Tool directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can I use this for my phone (Android/iPhone)?
    A: Yes. Most modern phones use high-quality OLED panels that are factory calibrated, but you can still use this tool to verify if your "Night Mode" or "True Tone" settings are shifting your colors too far. Tapping the "Full Screen" button is highly recommended on mobile to bypass browser UI elements.
  * Q: Why do my blacks look gray despite calibration?
    A: This is likely a limitation of your Panel Technology. Standard LCDs (IPS/TN) use a backlight that is always on. Even when a pixel is "black," some light leaks through (IPS Glow). True absolute blacks ($0.000$ nits) can only be achieved by OLED panels, where each pixel can be turned completely off.
  * Q: What is "Dynamic Contrast" and should I use it?
    A: Disable it immediately. Dynamic contrast (and "Eco-modes") constantly shifts the backlight based on what is on screen. This makes manual calibration impossible, as the reference patterns will shift as you look at them. Turn off all "Dynamic" enhancements before using this tool.

### Monitor Refresh Rate Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/monitor_refresh_tester
- Summary: The Pursuit of Fluidity: A Masterclass in Refresh Rates and Motion Artifacts In the digital era, the monitor is our primary window into virtual reality.

- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Monitor Refresh Rate Test directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why does the tool show 60 FPS on my 144Hz monitor?
    A: This is the most common Configuration Error. First, ensure your Windows/macOS display settings are actually set to 144Hz. Second, check your browser settings to ensure 'Hardware Acceleration' is enabled. Finally, many laptops will cap the browser at 60Hz when unplugged to save battery. Ensure you are in 'High Performance' mode.
  * Q: What is the difference between GtG and MPRT?
    A: GtG (Gray-to-Gray) measures the time it takes a pixel to change colors (ghosting). MPRT (Motion Picture Response Time) measures how long a pixel remains visible (blur). You can have a 0ms GtG monitor that still looks blurry because of the sample-and-hold persistence of a 60Hz refresh rate. To reduce blur, you need higher Hz or BFI. To reduce ghosting, you need better panel technology (IPS/OLED).
  * Q: Can I use this on my Android phone?
    A: Yes. Modern smartphones often have 90Hz or 120Hz displays. This Canvas tool is fully mobile-responsive and will detect the high-refresh capabilities of your mobile browser. It is a perfect way to test if your phone's 'Smooth Motion' setting is actually active or if it is dropping back to 60Hz due to thermal throttling.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Does this tool work on mobile phones (Android/iPhone)?
    A: Absolutely. Most modern smartphones use AMOLED or Super Retina displays, which are highly susceptible to burn-in (especially the status bar icons for Wi-Fi and Battery). To use this on Android, open this page in Chrome, tap the "Execute Scrubber" button, and the browser will automatically enter fullscreen mode to cover the entire panel.
  * Q: Can I run this on my Macbook or Laptop?
    A: Yes. While many laptops still use IPS LCD screens, high-end models (like the Macbook Pro or Dell XPS) use OLED or Mini-LED.   * Q: Is it safe to run the Scrubber overnight?
    A: We do not recommend running this overnight. The Scrubber drives pixels at high intensity to clear retention. Long-term exposure (8+ hours) can generate significant heat. We suggest limit sessions to 120 minutes. If the retention hasn't improved after two hours, the damage is likely permanent hardware degradation.

### OLED Screen Uniformity Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/oled_burnin_protector
- Summary: Panel Lottery: A Scientific Guide to OLED Diagnostics OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) technology represents the current pinnacle of consumer display science.
- Overview: OLED Screen Uniformity Test is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies.   * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: I see a faint line on 5% Grey. Is my TV broken?
    A: Almost certainly not. 95% of OLED panels have some level of vertical banding on the 5% grey slide. The "Normal Content Rule" applies: if you cannot see the line while watching a dark movie scene (like a night sky or shadow), then your panel is within spec. Only return a TV if the banding is visible during actual movie/game usage.
  * Q: How long does burn-in take to appear?
    A: Modern OLED panels are highly resistant. It typically requires thousands of hours of static content at 100% brightness for permanent burn-in to occur. For normal usage (movies, varied gaming), your panel will likely last 7-10 years before any noticeable degradation occurs. Pro Tip: Use the 0% Black slide periodically; if you see any silhouettes there, it's just temporary retention (which goes away), not permanent burn-in.
  * Q: Does this tool work on Android or iPhone?
    A: Perfectly. Most modern flagship phones (iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, Pixel) use OLED screens. Use this tool in your mobile browser to check for "Status Bar Burn-in" (where the battery and clock icons live) or to inspect a refurbished phone purchase for defects. Tap any color to enter the full-screen mode.
