### Frame-Time CSV Benchmark Analyzer
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/frametime_csv_analyzer
- Summary: Analyze PresentMon and CapFrameX CSV logs to calculate average FPS, 1% lows, 0.1% lows, and micro-stutter variance with interactive visual graphs.
- Overview: Analyze hardware frame-time benchmark logs from PresentMon, CapFrameX, and MSI Afterburner CSV files. Computes Average FPS, 1% Lows, 0.1% Lows, and micro-stutter percentage with interactive SVG graphs executed locally in browser memory.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Comprehensive 1% and 0.1% Low FPS Metrics
  * Interactive SVG Frame-Time Timeline Chart
  * Micro-Stutter Detection (>2.5x Mean Interval)
  * Instant Markdown Benchmark Summary Copy
- Procedure Steps:
  * Upload CSV Benchmark File: Select or drag your PresentMon or CapFrameX CSV benchmark file.
  * Review Computed Metrics: Inspect Average FPS, 1% Lows, frame-time variance, and total frame counts.
  * Inspect Stutter Graph: Examine the interactive frame-time timeline to pinpoint sudden frame drops and pacing spikes.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why are 1% Lows and 0.1% Lows more important than Average FPS?
    A: Average FPS masks intermittent stutter. A game running at 100 FPS average can still feel choppy if sudden 50ms frame delivery stalls occur. 1% and 0.1% lows measure the worst 1% and 0.1% of frame delivery times, directly reflecting perceptual smoothness.
  * Q: Which benchmarking utilities produce compatible CSV files?
    A: The analyzer automatically identifies headers from Intel PresentMon, CapFrameX, MSI Afterburner / RivaTuner (RTSS), and Fraps CSV outputs.
  * Q: What is considered a micro-stutter in this tool?
    A: A frame delivery interval that exceeds 2.5 times the run mean frame time is classified as an anomalous stutter event.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: How does the tool detect unmasked GPU vendor strings?
    A: Modern browsers provide the WEBGL_debug_renderer_info extension within WebGL contexts, allowing web applications to query the actual underlying graphics chipset (e.g. NVIDIA GeForce RTX, AMD Radeon, or Apple M-series) rather than generic driver wrappers.
  * Q: Does this test identify HDR monitor support?
    A: Yes. The tool queries CSS media features including dynamic-range: high and color-gamut: p3 to determine whether your monitor and operating system have High Dynamic Range enabled.
  * Q: Can this report be used to diagnose gaming performance issues?
    A: Yes. Verifying display refresh rates, hardware AV1/VP9 decode capabilities, and GPU driver strings helps detect mismatched display cable limits or integrated GPU fallback problems.

- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why does my controller only show up after I press a button?
    A: This is a Security Protocol built into modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Opera). To prevent websites from secretly tracking your connected devices, the Gamepad API is "locked" until the user explicitly interacts with the device. Pressing any button (A, X, Start) serves as your "Consent" to allow this specific tab to read your controller data.
  * Q: What is a 'Good' circularity error score?
    A: For a standard Xbox or PlayStation controller, an error between 8% and 15% is completely normal and expected. If you have a high-end Hall Effect controller (like a GuliKit or 8BitDo Ultimate), you should aim for a score below 1%. High circularity error in racing games means you might not be achieving full steering lock in diagonal turns.
  * Q: Does this work on my Android phone?
    A: Perfectly. Android has native support for Xbox and PlayStation controllers via Bluetooth or USB-OTG. The Gamepad Drift Visualizer is optimized for mobile browsers. You can connect your controller, open this Canvas page, and perform a full diagnostic while sitting on your couch or on the go.

### Keyboard Ghosting Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/nkey_rollover_tester

- Overview: Keyboard Ghosting Test is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies.   * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Does N-Key Rollover matter for work?
    A: Linguistically and practically, yes. While most people only type one key at a time, very fast typists ($120+$ WPM) often have 'overlapping' keypresses where they hit the second key before releasing the first. A keyboard with poor rollover will drop these characters, resulting in typos that aren't your fault. Professional-grade NKRO ensures a 1:1 relationship between your intent and the digital record.
  * Q: Can I use this to test my Android phone's keyboard?
    A: The N-Key Rollover Tester is fully responsive for Android, but most mobile touchscreens are limited by the Multi-Touch capacity of the screen (usually 10 points) rather than an electrical matrix. You can use this tool to verify how many fingers your mobile device can track simultaneously, which is critical for mobile rhythm games or complex gestures.
  * Q: Why do some key combinations fail on my 2KRO board?
    A: This is caused by Jamming. On a cheap matrix, three keys might share the same horizontal and vertical electrical pathways. If you press two of them, the third becomes invisible to the controller. High-end manufacturers optimize their matrix grid to ensure that common gaming clusters (like WASD or Arrow Keys) are on separate pathways to minimize jamming even without full NKRO.

### Keyboard Latency Test
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/keyboard_latency_test
- Summary: The Physics of Presence: A Masterclass in Input Latency In the digital domain, "lag" is the primary friction point between human intent and machine execution.
- Overview: Keyboard Latency Test is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Keyboard Latency Test directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Can this tool detect 8,000Hz polling?
    A: In a browser environment, no. Browser input handling is capped by the event loop and the OS polling rate. Even with an 8,000Hz keyboard, the Minimum Latency you see here will be bound by the browser's ability to fire the event and the monitor's frame rate. This tool is designed to measure Real-World Usage Latency (what you actually feel), not raw hardware micro-benchmarks that only an oscilloscope can capture.
  * Q: Why is my "Minimum" lower than 1ms?
    A: This usually indicates that the browser is "batching" events. If you press multiple keys very quickly, the OS may send them to the browser in a single packet. This causes performance.now() to read a delta that is lower than the actual hardware speed. To get the most accurate result, type at a steady, moderate pace rather than smashing the keys.
  * Q: Does this work on Android or Tablet?
    A: Perfectly. The meter supports physical keyboards connected via USB-OTG or Bluetooth on Android. Note that mobile operating systems have much higher background overhead than desktops, so you should expect higher Average Latency scores (30ms - 60ms) even on high-end hardware.

### Mouse Polling Rate Test (Hz) & Jitter Benchmark
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/mouse_polling_rate_hz
- Summary: Measure mouse polling rate in Hz, track interval jitter, and verify USB-IF stability thresholds. Runs locally in your browser with exportable reports.
- Overview: Test your mouse polling rate in Hertz (Hz) and interval jitter directly in your browser. Move your cursor continuously across the canvas to sample high-resolution hardware timestamps, verify sensor stability, and identify USB micro-stutter without installing background software.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Select Target Polling Rate: Choose your mouse configured polling rate (e.g. 500Hz, 1000Hz, or 8000Hz) and connection type (wired or 2.4GHz wireless).
  * Move Mouse in Circles: Move your cursor rapidly in continuous circles inside the designated test canvas to generate high-frequency PointerEvents.
  * Inspect Real-Time Readout: Observe live Hz output, peak frequency, geometric mean, and standard deviation jitter against USB-IF HID stability specifications.
  * Export Benchmark Report: Click 'Copy Benchmark Report' to copy an audited hardware summary with timestamps and jitter metrics to your clipboard.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is a good mouse polling rate for gaming?
    A: 1000 Hz (1ms interval) is the competitive standard for modern gaming. 500 Hz (2ms) is also stable. 4000Hz-8000Hz requires high-end multi-core CPUs and 240Hz+ monitors to avoid CPU-bound micro-stutter.
  * Q: Can web browsers accurately measure 4000Hz and 8000Hz polling rates?
    A: Modern Chromium browsers on desktop support high-resolution PointerEvents and performance.now() microsecond timestamps. However, OS scheduler load, display refresh rates, and browser event loop coalescing can induce minor jitter at 4000Hz+.
  * Q: Why does my mouse polling rate fluctuate or drop below 1000Hz?
    A: Common causes include using front-panel USB hubs sharing bus bandwidth, Windows USB power saving (selective suspend), high CPU interrupts (DPC latency), or moving the mouse too slowly to saturate USB reports.

### Mouse True DPI & CPI Deviation Benchmark
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/mouse_dpi_deviation_analyzer
- Summary: The Science of Mouse CPI Deviation, Optical Sensor Focal Planes, and Angle Snapping Direct Answer: What is Mouse CPI Deviation?
- Overview: Mouse True DPI & CPI Deviation Benchmark is a browser-based utility developed for professionals requiring immediate results without server dependencies. It executes all calculations locally on your client device using modern Web APIs, ensuring that your inputs, files, and diagnostic data remain within browser memory. No registration or software installation is required.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Local Browser Processing
  * Instant Calculation
  * no server uploads & Zero Logging
  * Works Offline in Browser Memory
- Procedure Steps:
  * Open Tool: Launch Mouse True DPI & CPI Deviation Benchmark directly in your browser on ToolkitGen. No account creation or installation needed.
  * Configure Input: Input your data, adjust slider parameters, or upload files directly into the client-side workspace.
  * Instant Calculation: Review real-time calculations or interactive visualizations generated on-device with instant local execution.
  * Export or Copy: Copy results to clipboard or download files with direct browser download and no data upload.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why does my mouse feel faster on the same DPI after changing mouse feet?
    A: Thicker aftermarket mouse skates (e.g. 0.85mm vs 0.70mm stock) raise the sensor aperture further from the mousepad. This height increase alters the lens magnification ratio, projecting a smaller surface area across the CMOS sensor and producing more coordinate counts per inch of travel (positive CPI deviation).
  * Q: What is mouse angle snapping and why is it harmful in FPS games?
    A: Angle snapping (also known as prediction) is a firmware smoothing algorithm that clamps near-horizontal or near-vertical diagonal hand motions into rigid 0° or 90° lines. While helpful in office applications, angle snapping actively prevents micro-adjustments onto enemy heads positioned on subtle elevation angles in CS2 and Valorant.
  * Q: Is an everyday credit card accurate enough to calibrate mouse DPI?
    A: Yes. Under the international ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 standard, banking cards, driver's licenses, and identification cards are strictly manufactured to dimensions of 85.60 mm (width) by 53.98 mm (height) with sub-millimeter tolerances, providing an exceptionally accurate, zero-cost physical reference available in any wallet.

  * Q: Why does my phone vibrate differently on different apps?
    A: Different developers use different Haptic Design Patterns. High-end apps use variable-frequency LRAs to create distinct sensations. A banking app might use a "Soft Click" for successful login, while a game uses a "Harsh Grumble" for an explosion. This tool allows you to isolate the hardware and prove that the vibration difference is caused by software logic, not a mechanical defect.

  * Q: Can the stress test damage my phone?
    A: The Vibration API is built with safety buffers by the browser manufacturer. However, haptic motors are moving parts. Running the Continuous Stress Test for excessive periods (over 10 minutes) could theoretically cause minor internal heat buildup. We recommend using the test for 30-60 seconds to perform an acoustic audit and then halting the cycle.

## Category: Health & Biometrics

### Long Gaming Session Planner
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/long_gaming_session_planner
- Summary: Structure extended gaming sessions with 20-20-20 visual rest intervals, scheduled hydration checkpoints, and ergonomic stretch routines.
- Overview: The Long Gaming Session Planner generates an evidence-based interval schedule for extended sedentary gameplay, calculating 20-20-20 visual breaks to prevent ciliary muscle spasm, baseline metabolic hydration targets, and hourly movement intervals. It includes an interactive browser session timer that runs locally on your device without server communication.
- Key Capabilities:
  * 20-20-20 Rule Interval Calculation
  * Metabolic Sedentary Hydration Sizing
  * Hourly Physical Movement and Stretch Checkpoints
  * Local Browser Session Audio/Visual Interval Timer
- Procedure Steps:
  * Set Planned Duration: Select your intended gaming session length in hours using the slider or duration buttons.
  * Review Generated Schedule: Inspect the breakdown of eye rest pauses, physical movement intervals, and target water intake.
  * Start Session Timer: Click Start Session Timer to activate client-side interval reminders directly in your browser.
  * Follow Interval Prompts: Take periodic distance rests every 20 minutes and complete physical stretches during designated checkpoints.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is the 20-20-20 rule and why is it effective?
    A: The 20-20-20 rule was developed by optometrist Dr. Jeffrey Anshel: every 20 minutes, focus your eyes on an object at least 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. Looking into the distance allows the ciliary muscles inside the eyes to completely relax, preventing digital eye strain and accommodation fatigue.
  * Q: Why does hydration matter during sedentary gaming?
    A: Prolonged concentration reduces blink rates from an average of 15-20 blinks per minute down to 5-7 blinks per minute, accelerating corneal tear evaporation. Maintaining systemic hydration supports tear film stability and cognitive alertness without reliance on high-sugar energy drinks.
  * Q: How often should I stand up during a multi-hour session?
    A: Ergonomics specialists recommend standing, walking, or performing gentle joint mobilization for 3 to 5 minutes every 60 minutes. Brief posture breaks restore venous blood return from the lower extremities and decompress lumbar spinal discs.

## Category: Input / Peripherals

### Mouse and Touchscreen Tester
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/mouse_touch_tester
- Summary: Test mouse switches for double-click chatter, measure click speed CPS, inspect scroll wheel delta, and verify multi-touch input points locally.
- Overview: Diagnose mechanical mouse switch chatter (unwanted double clicking), measure click speed (Clicks Per Second), test scroll wheel direction stability, and track multi-touch screen coordinates. All input testing executes locally with microsecond timestamp logging.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Switch Chatter Detection (Sub-75ms Bounce Detection)
  * Real-Time Clicks Per Second (CPS) Speed Counter
  * Scroll Wheel Delta & Inversion Direction Meter
  * Multi-Touch Canvas Tracking with Coordinate Display
- Procedure Steps:
  * Select Test Mode: Choose between Mouse Switch Chatter Test, Click Speed CPS, or Touchscreen Canvas.
  * Perform Input Actions: Click the test zone, scroll your wheel, or place multiple fingers on the touch surface.
  * Review Hardware Verdict: Inspect detected chatter events, maximum CPS scores, and touch tracking coordinates.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: What is mouse switch chatter and what causes it?
    A: Mechanical mouse switches rely on microscopic metal leaf springs. Over millions of actuations, contact oxidation or metal fatigue causes the contacts to bounce upon release, registering an unintentional second click within 20ms to 75ms.
  * Q: How does the chatter detector distinguish intentional double clicks?
    A: Human finger muscles rarely complete a deliberate double click in under 80 milliseconds. A click registration occurring under 75 milliseconds from switch release is mathematically classified as hardware switch chatter.
  * Q: Does this tool support mouse side buttons and scroll wheel clicks?
    A: Yes. The interface tracks Left Click (Button 0), Middle Click (Button 1), Right Click (Button 2), and Browser Forward/Back buttons (Buttons 3 & 4).

## Category: Hardware / Storage

### ZFS RAID Capacity Calculator
- URL: https://toolkitgen.com/tool/zfs_raid_calculator
- Summary: Calculate usable storage capacity, parity overhead, and 80% pool fill limits for ZFS RAIDZ1, RAIDZ2, RAIDZ3, and mirrors with vdev planning.
- Overview: Calculate true usable storage capacity, parity disk overhead, and recommended 80% maximum pool fill thresholds for OpenZFS and TrueNAS pools. Supports Stripe, 2-Way Mirror, RAIDZ1, RAIDZ2, and RAIDZ3 configurations with exact TB to TiB conversions.
- Key Capabilities:
  * Comprehensive VDEV Configurations (RAIDZ1, RAIDZ2, RAIDZ3, Mirrors)
  * Decimal TB (10^12) to Binary TiB (2^40) Storage Conversion
  * 80% Pool Fill Limit and Performance Degradation Warning
  * SLOG and L2ARC Cache Sizing Guidance
- Procedure Steps:
  * Select Drive Count & Size: Specify the quantity and commercial capacity (in TB) of your storage drives.
  * Choose Redundancy Profile: Select Stripe, 2-Way Mirror, RAIDZ1 (1-disk parity), RAIDZ2 (2-disk parity), or RAIDZ3 (3-disk parity).
  * Review Usable Capacity: Inspect raw capacity vs true usable TiB, parity overhead, and the critical 80% safe fill limit.
- Frequent Questions:
  * Q: Why is usable ZFS capacity less than raw drive manufacturer size?
    A: Drive manufacturers market drives using decimal terabytes (1 TB = 1,000,000,000,000 bytes), whereas ZFS and operating systems allocate space in binary tebibytes (1 TiB = 1,099,511,627,776 bytes). Additionally, ZFS reserves ~3% slop space for internal metadata and copy-on-write overhead.
  * Q: Why is the 80% pool capacity rule important in ZFS?
    A: ZFS uses a copy-on-write transaction model. When a pool exceeds 80% capacity, the space allocator switches from first-fit to best-fit algorithms, resulting in severe write performance degradation and fragmentation.
  * Q: What is the minimum recommended drive count for RAIDZ2?
    A: While RAIDZ2 can function with 4 drives, 6 to 8 drives per vdev is standard engineering practice to balance parity overhead (33% to 25%) with high fault tolerance.
